device.name: simpler-env GraspSingleCokeCanInScene-v0 (static Google robot picks a coke can)

facts.text: GraspSingleCokeCanInScene-v0 is registered with max_episode_steps=80 and its constructor fixes model_ids to ['coke_can']
The default robot is google_robot_static
The static Google robot's default control mode is arm_pd_ee_delta_pose_align_interpolate_by_planner_gripper_pd_joint_target_delta_pos_interpolate_by_planner
The arm controller takes a position lower bound of -1.0, a position upper bound of 1.0 and a rotation bound of pi/2
The arm action is a Box of three position and three rotation elements built from those bounds
A controller configured with normalize_action=True receives a Box with bounds -1 and 1
The selected gripper controller has use_target=True and clip_target=True
The combined controller flattens the controllers' Box spaces into one Box action space
A controller with use_target reports its target_qpos as its controller state
The default simulation frequency is 500 Hz and the default control frequency is 20 Hz
The control timestep is the reciprocal of the control frequency, so 50 ms at the default 20 Hz
step returns the observation, the reward, the terminated flag, a False truncation flag and info
The default observation mode is state and get_obs flattens the state dict into one array
The state observation puts the agent proprioception and the task extras under agent and extra
The agent proprioception is qpos, qvel and the controller state
A static Google robot has 11 qpos values
The agent observation adds the robot base pose
The task extras add the tcp pose, the object pose and the object-minus-tcp position
The reward is 1.0 when info['success'] is true and 0.0 otherwise
Success requires a grasp and lifting the object more than 0.01 above its settled height
get_done returns info['success'], so the episode terminates when the object is lifted
gym.make wraps the environment in a TimeLimit when max_episode_steps is set
A reset draws the object xy uniformly from [-0.35, -0.02] to [-0.12, 0.42] and drops it from 0.5 above the table height
A reset draws the static Google base x from 0.30 to 0.40 and y from 0.0 to 0.2 unless the reset options give an initial xy

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the initial state and the dynamics are deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; upstream draws with numpy RandomState and this package's fake with Python's random.Random, so a seed gives different trajectories on the two

gaps: the fake backend is a toy kinematic stand-in, not the SAPIEN physics of the upstream environment: no rigid-body dynamics, contact solving, gripper geometry, asset loading or camera rendering
the observation has the 47-number layout of the default state mode, but its values are placeholders; image, state_dict and point-cloud observation modes are not served
the fake draws with Python's random.Random and upstream with numpy RandomState, so one seed gives different trajectories on the two
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms (50 ms) only
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state or set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
